title: Faith as faithfulness
hookLine: faith is also showing up, again and again
tomorrow: Year four close: the many rooms

lines: A LAW SIGNED: PRAY TO NO ONE.
cards: An open window, facing Jerusalem. A new law has just been signed: for thirty days, anyone who prays to any god or man except the king goes to the lions. Daniel knows it's signed.

He goes home, up to his room, where the windows are open toward Jerusalem. And the Book of Daniel says he "kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime."
As he did aforetime. No speech, no protest. He just keeps doing what he did before, at the window, in plain sight.

teach.b: Yesterday's Greek word, pistis, meant trust. It also means faithfulness: keeping faith, the way you keep a promise or keep showing up for a friend.

teach.h: THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT: FAITH.
teach.b: When Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit, the King James Bible reads: "love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith." Faith, on a list of ways a person acts, right beside gentleness and goodness.
Here it reads like faithfulness: something you keep doing. Trust is leaning your weight on someone. Faithfulness is coming back, again and again, whether or not you feel it that day.
And one old song puts God's faithfulness before ours. Lamentations is a book of grief, sung over a city in ruins.

This path heard the line a few weeks ago; this time, listen for its last word: "It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."
Faithfulness, in that line, isn't a feeling. It's what shows up the next day, and the next.
The second letter to Timothy has a line for days when faith gives out: "If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself." After these weeks of grief and doubt, that line has a job.
On a day when you can't feel trust at all, you can still be faithful. You can come back to the window. Daniel's prayer wasn't proof that he felt brave.
It was what he did aforetime, done once more.

how: Some Christians practice faithfulness through regular habits: daily prayer at set times, weekly worship, and keeping promises such as marriage vows and baptismal vows, including through seasons when faith feels dry.

o: a vow to God you must keep without ever slipping
a strong feeling of being sure, felt every single day
coming back again and again, whether you feel it or not

games.q: you're Daniel. the law is signed: pray to anyone but the king and you go to the lions. what do you do?
o: pray in secret, with the windows shut.
stop praying until the thirty days are over.
pray at your open window, as you did before.
games.why: he kneels at his open window toward Jerusalem, three times a day, as he did aforetime. nothing new: he just keeps showing up.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you used to do faithfully and have let slip, a call, a walk, a prayer, a page of reading, a promise to yourself, and look at it without scolding, the way Daniel looked at his open window.
Choose one small way back, smaller than you think it needs to be. If you pray, you can say, great is thy faithfulness; if you don't, simply notice that you showed up here, today.

wordCard.voice: Faith as faithfulness. Pistis as keeping faith: coming back again and again, like Daniel at his window, held up by a faithfulness that is new every morning.

orig.note: Greek: faith, and also faithfulness. in the King James list of the fruit of the Spirit it is translated faith.

carryVoice: Your line: keep showing up. Not perfectly, just as you did aforetime. That's today, done.
